key_insight: A Monte Carlo framework can turn published aggregate trial results into patient-level risk predictions for rare cancers, demonstrated here in Ewing sarcoma.
clinical_relevance: It may help refine survivorship surveillance and future trial stratification, but it is not ready to replace individual clinical judgment or prospective validation.
method: Six-stage discrete-event simulation combines genetic risk, serial biomarker dynamics, ctDNA-MRD, and competing mortality risks.
Adverse-effect modules project long-term toxicity across five organ systems from chemo and radiation exposure.
Genotype-conditional weighting improves subgroup discrimination versus equal weighting.
evidence_signal: In published Ewing sarcoma data from more than 3,400 patients, the model reported 3.2% mean absolute error across 23 efficacy endpoints and stayed within confidence intervals for all 20 toxicity endpoints.
watch_item: The approach was validated against aggregate published data and remains a hypothesis for transfer to other rare cancers until prospective patient-level validation is available.
paper_title: WITHDRAWN: Multi-Timepoint Risk Stratification in Rare Cancers: A Computational Framework Validated against Published Ewing Sarcoma Trial Data
